description: A calculus module: three gained inputs summed and slew limited, then offered as a differential and as three forms of integral

params.text: Sets the gain on the summed inputs; the knob is marked in decibels but moves three times as far, -72dB at fully counter-clockwise to 18dB fully clockwise
Sets the corner of the slew limiting low pass, four octaves either side of C4 at 261.63Hz
Sets the time step the integrals work over, a four thousandth of a sample at fully counter-clockwise up to one whole sample fully clockwise
Sets that input's level into the sum; the centre of its travel passes nothing and the two ends pass plus and minus one and a half times

inputs.text: Moves the gain on top of the dB knob, a tenth of a doubling per volt
Moves the slew corner one octave per volt on top of the Hz knob
Moves the integral time step on top of its knob, one doubling per volt, through the same low pass the knob goes through
One of the three signals summed, at the level its own gain knob sets

outputs.text: The cube root of the first differential of the summed signal
The cube root of the summed signal divided by the time step, which is the form the 1/Sigma integral works from
The cube root of the summed signal multiplied by the time step, which is the form the LN Sigma integral works from
The cube root of the plain integral of the summed signal
The cube root of the integral taken in its pole form
The cube root of the integral taken in its logarithmic form

notes: every output is a cube root, which is what holds these estimates inside a usable voltage range
an output is only computed while a cable is patched to it, so an unpatched jack carries 0V rather than a held value
the half-life knob is configured with a default outside its own range, so where it stands on a new module is decided by Rack rather than by the module
